docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
After installation, AWX needs to be configured with:

  1. Credentials — SSH key to connect to worker nodes
  2. Inventory — List of servers to manage
  3. Project — Link to GitHub playbook repository
  4. Job Template — Combine all above and run!

docs.title: Step 1 — Add Credentials
docs.text:
Credentials tell AWX how to SSH into your worker nodes.

  1. Click Credentials on left menu
  2. Click Add
  3. Fill in:
Field Value Name Worker-SSH-Key Organization Default Credential Type Machine SSH Private Key Paste contents of key.pem
  1. Click Save

Tip

Get your key contents with: cat key.pem Copy everything including BEGIN and END lines.

docs.title: Step 2 — Create Inventory
docs.text:
Inventory tells AWX which servers to manage.

  1. Click Inventories on left menu
  2. Click Add then Add Inventory
  3. Fill in:
Field Value Name Worker-Nodes Organization Default
  1. Click Save

docs.title: Add Hosts
docs.text:
1. Click on Worker-Nodes inventory
  2. Click Hosts tab
  3. Click Add for each worker:

Server 1: 

Name: Server1
Variables:
  ansible_host: worker-1-ip
  ansible_user: ec2-user

Server 2: 

Name: Server2
Variables:
  ansible_host: worker-2-ip
  ansible_user: ec2-user

docs.title: Add Group
docs.text:
Warning

This step is critical! Without a group your playbook will not match any hosts and nothing will run!

  1. Click Groups tab
  2. Click Add
  3. Name it exactly: webservers
  4. Click Save
  5. Click on webservers group
  6. Click Hosts tab
  7. Click Add existing host
  8. Add both Server1 and Server2

docs.title: Step 3 — Create Project
docs.text:
Project links AWX to your GitHub repository.

  1. Click Projects on left menu
  2. Click Add
  3. Fill in:
Field Value Name Ansible-Webserver-Project Organization Default Source Control Type Git Source Control URL https://github.com/keneanyaragbu/ansible-webservers Branch main
  1. Check Update Revision on Launch
  2. Click Save

Success

A green circle confirms successful sync with GitHub

docs.title: Step 4 — Create Job Template
docs.text:
Job Template combines everything into one runnable job.

  1. Click Templates on left menu
  2. Click Add then Add Job Template
  3. Fill in:
Field Value Name Deploy-Webserver Job Type Run Inventory Worker-Nodes Project Ansible-Webserver-Project Playbook webserver.yml Credentials Worker-SSH-Key
  1. Click Save
  2. Click Launch

docs.title: Step 5 — Verify Deployment
docs.text:
After job completes check:

  • Job status shows Successful
  • Tasks show changed not skipping
  • Open browser at worker node IP
  • Webpage shows updated content

docs.title: Workflow Summary
docs.text:
Edit code on GitHub
        ↓
AWX pulls latest code automatically
        ↓
Ansible playbook executes across servers
        ↓
Both servers updated simultaneously
        ↓
Live webpage updated!

docs.title: Step 1 — Install Dependencies
docs.text:
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y git curl wget python3 python3-pip

docs.title: Step 2 — Install Docker
docs.text:
sudo apt install -y docker.io
sudo systemctl start docker
sudo systemctl enable docker

docs.title: Step 3 — Install K3s
docs.text:
curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | sh -
export KUBECONFIG=/etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml
echo "export KUBECONFIG=/etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml" >> ~/.bashrc

Verify K3s is running: 

kubectl get nodes

Expected output: NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION ip-172-xx-xx-xx Ready control-plane 98s v1.34.6+k3s1

docs.title: Step 4 — Create AWX Namespace
docs.text: kubectl create namespace awx

docs.title: Step 5 — Deploy AWX Operator
docs.text: kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ansible/awx-operator/devel/deploy/awx-operator.yaml -n awx

docs.title: Step 6 — Fix Image Registry Issue
docs.text:
Warning

gcr.io has been deprecated. You must replace the image with quay.io

kubectl edit deployment awx-operator-controller-manager -n awx

Change: gcr.io/kubebuilder/kube-rbac-proxy:v0.15.0

To: quay.io/brancz/kube-rbac-proxy:v0.15.0

Save with Esc then :wq

docs.title: Step 7 — Verify Operator is Running
docs.text:
kubectl get pods -n awx

Expected: NAME READY STATUS awx-operator-controller-manager-ccbc476dc-gvgjz 2/2 Running

docs.title: Step 8 — Deploy AWX Instance
docs.text:
kubectl apply -f awx-instance.yml

Contents of awx-instance.yml: 

apiVersion: awx.ansible.com/v1beta1
kind: AWX
metadata:
  name: awx
  namespace: awx
spec:
  service_type: nodeport

docs.title: Step 9 — Watch Pods Come Up
docs.text:
kubectl get pods -n awx --watch

Wait until all pods show Running: awx-migration Completed awx-operator 2/2 Running awx-postgres-15 1/1 Running awx-task 4/4 Running awx-web 3/3 Running

docs.title: Step 10 — Get NodePort
docs.text:
kubectl get svc -n awx

Look for: awx-service NodePort 10.43.x.x 80:30701/TCP

docs.title: Step 11 — Get Admin Password
docs.text:
kubectl get secret awx-admin-password -n awx \
-o jsonpath="{.data.password}" | base64 --decode && echo ""

docs.title: Step 12 — Access AWX Web UI
docs.text: http://:30701 Username: admin Password: (from Step 11)

docs.title: What is AWX?
docs.text: AWX is the open source version of Red Hat Ansible Tower. It provides a web-based user interface, REST API, and task engine built on top of Ansible. It is the enterprise way of managing Ansible at scale.

docs.title: Project Goal
docs.text: Deploy AWX on a lightweight Kubernetes cluster (K3s) on AWS EC2 and use it to orchestrate Ansible playbook execution across multiple managed worker nodes.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: AWX Web UI (Browser) ↓ AWX Server (Ubuntu EC2 - t2.large) ├── K3s (Lightweight Kubernetes) │ └── AWX Operator │ ├── awx-web (Web UI) │ ├── awx-task (Job Execution) │ └── awx-postgres (Database) ↓ Worker Nodes (Amazon Linux EC2) ├── Server 1 (54.157.103.132) └── Server 2 (100.54.72.121)

docs.title: Issue 1 — ImagePullBackOff
docs.text:
Symptom: Failed to pull image "gcr.io/kubebuilder/kube-rbac-proxy:v0.15.0": not found

Cause: Google Container Registry (gcr.io) has been deprecated.

Fix: 

kubectl edit deployment awx-operator-controller-manager -n awx
Replace: gcr.io/kubebuilder/kube-rbac-proxy:v0.15.0 With: quay.io/brancz/kube-rbac-proxy:v0.15.0

docs.title: Issue 2 — No Hosts Matched
docs.text:
Symptom: Could not match supplied host pattern, ignoring: webservers skipping: no hosts matched

Cause: Hosts were added individually to inventory but not assigned to a group called webservers.

Fix: 1. Go to Inventories → Worker-Nodes 2. Click Groups tab 3. Add group named webservers 4. Add both hosts to the group 5. Relaunch job template

docs.title: Issue 3 — AWX Shows Success But Nothing Changed
docs.text:
Symptom: Job shows green Success but servers not updated.

Cause: AWX reports success even when no hosts are matched.

Fix: Always check job output for:

  • changed → tasks actually ran ✅
  • ok → already configured, no change needed
  • skipping → hosts not matched ⚠️

docs.title: Issue 4 — Permission Denied on SSH Key
docs.text:
Symptom: WARNING: UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE! Permissions 0644 for key.pem are too open.

Fix: 

chmod 400 key.pem
